claims.text: Increasing molybdenum content in CoCrFeNi-based high-entropy-alloy composites will reduce the coefficient of friction over a wide temperature range.
Increasing molybdenum content in CoCrFeNi-based high-entropy-alloy composites will reduce the wear rate over a wide temperature range.
The initial composite has low molybdenum content.
The initial composite lacks optimized self-lubricating secondary phases.
Increasing molybdenum during spark-plasma-sintering fabrication promotes the formation of beneficial lubricating phases.
Suitable processing conditions can enable formation of Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite phases.
Increased molybdenum content facilitates formation of MoS2 phases.
Increased molybdenum content may improve the dispersion of Ag and Cr2O3 phases within the composite.
Increased molybdenum content may improve the stability of Ag and Cr2O3 phases within the composite.
Higher molybdenum levels promote in-situ generation of lubricious MoS2 layers.
Higher molybdenum levels enhance the stability of oxide phases.
The resulting self-lubricating layer reduces friction.
Improved mechanical integrity lowers wear.
The low-molybdenum baseline composite has higher friction and wear rates than the proposed molybdenum-enriched composite under similar test conditions.
The beneficial effect requires a compositional and processing window that permits proper formation of Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 phases.
Deviations from the required compositional or processing window may prevent formation of the intended self-lubricating microstructure.
The proposed qualitative mechanism and improvements are supported by prior compositional-variation studies.
The magnitude of friction and wear reduction may vary with processing conditions and loading environments.
A failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in both friction coefficient and wear rate across the tested temperatures would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to detect the expected lubricious phases would falsify the hypothesis.
